steps.speaker: Paper Effigy
steps.content: Sssss—
Your shackles lash out. The paper effigy shrieks—a thin, tearing sound—and shatters into fragments. You don't hesitate. You slip past its remains and run, desperate for escape.
But despair crashes down moments later. The path ahead is gone. Erased. In its place stands a wall of impenetrable darkness, waiting for you to step into its depths.
Behind you, the fragments stir, reforming. One becomes two. Two becomes four... The resurrected effigies drag their bodies across the ground, pulling themselves toward you.

steps.speaker: Paper Effigy
steps.content: You'll never find your way out alone. Beg me, and I'll show you the path. All it takes is a single plea—

steps.speaker: Stone Lion
steps.content: Hehehehehe...
Around you, the paper effigies and stone statues multiply. And with each passing moment, your limbs grow heavier. Heavier. As if your very flesh is turning to stone from the inside out.
You have to move. You have to escape. Whatever these things are, they're pulling you under, and if you stay any longer, you'll become one of them. Trapped and frozen forever.
I will not... let you keep me here!

Your body fails you mid-motion. You crumple, and the moment you strike the ground, you hear a dull, heavy thud of stone meeting earth. You force your head around, muscles screaming, only to see a swarm of paper effigies and red-threaded lions closing in—
Tinkle—!
A single bell note rings out, pure and sharp, and the fog recoils. Pale blue spectral flames erupt from the ground before you, cold fire roaring skyward.

The paper effigies ignite instantly, curling and shriveling like dead leaves in a furnace, and from their burning forms comes a sound that might almost be screaming. You look up, eyes wide, gaze traveling past the flames—
Mao, fei, bi, hong, he, yi, zhen, li, dui...

A mask conceals the upper half of the woman's face. Only her pale lips remain visible, shaping a mantra that means nothing to you. Each syllable falls deliberately as if the words themselves have weight.
She moves toward you, unhurried, stepping through the spectral flames as though they were solid ground. One side of her robe is dark with stain, but the fire does not touch her.
Heed my command... Let the fire take you.

The bell rises in her hand. She flicks her wrist, and the ringing swells, becoming something vast. The spectral flames leap to obey. They burn away the fog that has plagued you since the beginning. Those cold, watching eyes are gone, and the paper effigies curl and crumble to ash in the space of a heartbeat.

steps.speaker: Paper Effigy
steps.content: Screeeeech—
Her hands form another seal. In an instant, the red threads on the lions ignite. And when the last thread snaps, the stone beasts shatter completely.
The screams rise from the wreckage, anguished and terrible. The flames crackle and hiss. But gradually, inevitably, both fade into utter stillness.
Pant... Pant...
In that stillness, you see the woman slowly turn her head toward you.
Her skin holds no color, bloodless as bone. Long black hair spills down her back, drifting lazily in the fog, and the bell in her hand sways with each gentle movement.
Tinkle.
The familiar mask on her face catches your attention. Perhaps... she was part of the expedition too?
But then why the Eastian robe? Is the bell in her hand the source of those warning chimes? Has she been the one helping you all this time?

She approaches silently, making no sound at all. Her hand reaches toward you. Her sleeve drifts close, nearly brushing the tip of your nose. And you see her fingers: slender, yet vivid red like blood. Golden runes pulse across her skin, alive with light.
She doesn't notice your tension—or if she does, she gives no sign. She steps closer still.
The spectral flames still cling to her, flickering softly. As she draws near, tiny sparks drift free. They fall onto your hands, and you find them ice-cold.
You edge away, a quiet resolve settling over you: you would ask for nothing in this place ever again. Every kindness, it seems, comes with a hidden toll.
Her hand is cold. When you grasp it for leverage, it doesn't move at all, and she hauls you to your feet as if you weigh nothing.
You stay where you are, wary, your grip on the shackles hidden but ready. Still, she demands no price.
She lets go and retreats a single step. Her head tilts, just slightly—studying you, perhaps, though you can't be sure. Then, slowly, her lips part.
The divination did not lie... Here you are.
She gives a stiff nod, then lifts the bell in her hand and gives it a soft shake, as if to say there's nothing to fear.
Do you wish to leave?
I can be your guide... out of here.
You can't read her; her voice gives nothing away. But she saved you, and she's asked for nothing. Maybe that means something. Maybe... she's different from the paper effigies after all.
...You know the way out of here? Can you show me?
She nods once more, then turns and walks away.
As she recedes, the dispelled shadows rush back together, like ripples smoothing into stillness, but in reverse. Eager. Hungry. It seems her protection extends only to those who walk beside her.
She must sense you lingering, because she stops just ahead. Firelight flickers across her slender shape; the bell chimes, gentle and steady. In all this madness, she alone shines.
She is waiting.
With no better path in sight, you draw a breath and go to her.
Assured of your company, she presses on. Her bell pulses slow and deep, each chime pushing back the dark like ripples on black water.
—Clink.
Your foot strikes something. You look down and find the copper coin from before. This time, its reverse face stares up at you, and a sudden unease crawls over your skin.
Tinkle, tinkle, tinkle... The bell grows distant. She's pulling away. No time to think. You snatch the coin, pocket it, and hurry after her.
